what_this_cell_measures: An individual's economic security: income, savings, housing stability, and access to the material means of a decent life.
benefit_movement: More stable income, affordable housing, reduced debt, secured access to essentials.
harm_movement: Job loss, eviction risk, debt spirals, loss of essential goods or services.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: income and employment records; housing stability / eviction data; debt and arrears; cost-of-living and benefit uptake
gate_cues: Gate classes: Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare in most cases; can escalate to rights-covered where a subsistence or social-minimum floor is legally recognised.
example: Example: A wage policy that lifts low-income workers above a local living-wage line improves U1/D1.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether the income/housing change is measured against a declared baseline cohort, not anecdote.

what_this_cell_measures: The individual's physical and mental health, safety, and bodily integrity.
benefit_movement: Lower injury/illness risk, better access to care, improved mental health, safer conditions.
harm_movement: Injury, illness, untreated conditions, exposure to hazards, deteriorating mental health.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: morbidity / mortality data; care access and waiting times; injury and exposure records; validated mental-health measures
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Frequently rights-covered: bodily integrity and access-to-care floors can trigger NCRC. Severe individual harm escalates regardless of aggregate benefit.
example: Example: A treatment-access change that removes a barrier for a chronic-illness group improves U1/D2.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether a claimed health gain rests on outcome data or only on inputs (e.g. clinics built ≠ health improved).

what_this_cell_measures: The quality and stability of a person's close personal relationships and social connection.
benefit_movement: Stronger bonds, reduced isolation, more supportive networks.
harm_movement: Isolation, relationship breakdown, forced separation, loss of support.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: loneliness / connection surveys; support-network mapping; separation or displacement records
gate_cues: Gate classes: Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Usually ordinary welfare; measurement is often soft, so uncertainty should be marked explicitly.
example: Example: A relocation program that keeps support networks intact protects U1/D3.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer challenges whether a relationship claim is evidenced or inferred from a proxy like attendance.

what_this_cell_measures: The individual's access to education, skills, and the capacity to learn and develop.
benefit_movement: Better access to learning, skill gains, expanded opportunity.
harm_movement: Lost access to education, deskilling, barriers to learning.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: enrolment and completion; skills assessments; access and dropout data
gate_cues: Gate classes: Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; can touch rights where a basic-education entitlement exists.
example: Example: A reskilling program for displaced workers improves U1/D4.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether learning outcomes are demonstrated or only opportunity offered.

what_this_cell_measures: The person's real ability to choose, refuse, consent, act, and shape their own life path.
benefit_movement: More autonomy, better options, stronger consent, freedom from coercion and surveillance.
harm_movement: Coercion, manipulation, surveillance, forced dependency, loss of meaningful choice.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: consent quality; availability of alternatives / opt-out; coercion complaints; mobility and accessibility data; applicable legal protections
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Often rights-covered. Triggers NCRC when liberty, bodily integrity, due process, dignity, or information rights are impaired — non-compensatory regardless of welfare gains elsewhere.
example: Example: A transport policy that gives disabled residents reliable independent mobility improves U1/D5.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer tests whether consent was genuine and revocable, or merely formal.

what_this_cell_measures: The individual's sense of meaning, dignity, and worth in their life and work.
benefit_movement: Greater sense of purpose, recognition, dignity, and self-respect.
harm_movement: Humiliation, alienation, loss of role or recognition, indignity.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: dignity / recognition measures; role and identity surveys; qualitative testimony
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Can be rights-covered where human dignity is implicated; otherwise ordinary. Often hard to measure — mark uncertainty.
example: Example: A program that treats welfare recipients with dignified, non-stigmatising processes supports U1/D6.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer distinguishes a genuine dignity effect from sentiment unsupported by experience data.

what_this_cell_measures: The immediate physical environment a person lives in: air, noise, water, hazards, and surroundings.
benefit_movement: Cleaner air/water, less noise, fewer local hazards, healthier surroundings.
harm_movement: Pollution exposure, noise, contamination, environmental hazards near the person.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: local air/water/noise monitoring; hazard proximity; exposure records
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; can become rights-covered under environmental-health protections and disproportionate-exposure (environmental-justice) concerns.
example: Example: A factory buffer-zone rule that cuts a household's pollutant exposure improves U1/D7.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks measured exposure change against the affected location, not a city-wide average.

what_this_cell_measures: The economic security of the household unit: shared income, assets, housing, and ability to meet needs.
benefit_movement: Improved household finances, housing security, reduced shared debt.
harm_movement: Household impoverishment, housing loss, debt, inability to meet needs.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: household income and assets; housing tenure; arrears and food-security data
gate_cues: Gate classes: Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; escalates toward rights where dependents (children, disabled members) face a subsistence floor.
example: Example: A childcare subsidy that frees household income improves U2/D1.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether the household, not just the earner, is the measured unit.

what_this_cell_measures: The collective physical and mental health and safety of household members, including dependents.
benefit_movement: Better shared health, safer home, improved care for dependents and caregivers.
harm_movement: Household illness, unsafe housing, caregiver burnout, harm to dependents.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: household health surveys; home-safety inspections; caregiver-strain measures; dependent outcome data
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Frequently rights-covered where children or dependents are affected; child welfare can trigger NCRC. Caregiver harm is easily hidden — surface it.
example: Example: A home-care support program that reduces caregiver strain and improves a dependent's health raises U2/D2.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks that dependents and caregivers are scored separately, not blended into one household figure.

what_this_cell_measures: The strength, stability, and supportive quality of relationships within the household.
benefit_movement: Stronger family bonds, stability, reduced conflict, kept-together units.
harm_movement: Family breakdown, forced separation, household conflict, instability.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: family-stability surveys; separation / removal records; conflict indicators
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Can be rights-covered (family unity, child rights); otherwise ordinary. Measurement is soft — mark uncertainty.
example: Example: A policy that avoids unnecessary family separation in housing transitions protects U2/D3.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether a cohesion claim rests on outcomes or on assumed effects of a program.

what_this_cell_measures: The household's collective access to information, education, and learning capacity.
benefit_movement: Better shared access to education and information, intergenerational learning.
harm_movement: Loss of household educational access, information poverty.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: household connectivity / device access; children's schooling continuity; adult-learning access
gate_cues: Gate classes: Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; touches rights where basic-education entitlements for children apply.
example: Example: A home-broadband program that enables children's remote schooling improves U2/D4.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks access actually reaches the household, not just the area.

what_this_cell_measures: The household's collective ability to make decisions, plan, and control its own circumstances.
benefit_movement: Greater household self-determination, planning ability, freedom from external control.
harm_movement: Loss of household control, externally imposed decisions, dependency.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: decision-autonomy surveys; dependency / conditionality of support; forced-relocation data
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Can be rights-covered (family privacy, autonomy); otherwise ordinary.
example: Example: A flexible-benefit design that lets households allocate support to their own priorities raises U2/D5.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer tests whether household choice is real or constrained by conditions.

what_this_cell_measures: The household's shared sense of identity, belonging, dignity, and purpose.
benefit_movement: Stronger shared identity, belonging, dignity, and continuity.
harm_movement: Loss of household identity, stigma, indignity, eroded belonging.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: belonging / identity surveys; stigma indicators; qualitative testimony
gate_cues: Gate classes: Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Usually ordinary welfare; can touch dignity rights. Soft to measure — mark uncertainty.
example: Example: A culturally-respectful resettlement process preserves U2/D6.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer separates a real meaning effect from program rhetoric.

what_this_cell_measures: The physical environmental quality of the home and its immediate setting.
benefit_movement: Healthier home conditions, reduced indoor hazards, better surroundings.
harm_movement: Indoor pollution, mould, hazards, degraded immediate environment.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: housing-quality inspections; indoor air / damp measures; hazard records
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; rights-relevant under habitability standards.
example: Example: A retrofit program that removes household mould improves U2/D7.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks measured home conditions, not self-report alone.

what_this_cell_measures: The shared economic resources, infrastructure, and services available to a local community.
benefit_movement: Better local infrastructure, services, and economic opportunity.
harm_movement: Loss of services, infrastructure decay, local economic decline.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: local service provision; infrastructure condition; local employment / business data
gate_cues: Gate classes: Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; containment-relevant when local gains are extracted at the cost of wider scopes, or when shared infrastructure is hollowed out.
example: Example: A community facility upgrade that adds usable shared services improves U3/D1.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether the benefit is genuinely shared or captured by a subgroup.

what_this_cell_measures: The collective physical and mental health and safety of the local population.
benefit_movement: Lower community disease/injury burden, better local care access, safer environment.
harm_movement: Local disease spread, unsafe conditions, reduced care access, environmental health harm.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: local public-health surveillance; care-access data; injury / safety statistics; environmental-health monitoring
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Tail Risk; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare normally; rights-relevant under disproportionate harm or care-access floors; tail-relevant where local outbreaks or contamination could cascade.
example: Example: A clean-water intervention that cuts a community's disease burden improves U3/D2.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether subgroup harms are masked by a favourable community average.

what_this_cell_measures: The quality of trust, cooperation, belonging, safety, and relational fabric within a community.
benefit_movement: Increased trust, reduced isolation, better cooperation, stronger neighbourhood resilience.
harm_movement: Polarisation, exclusion, displacement, fear, social fragmentation.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: community trust surveys; participation rates; crime / fear-of-crime data; displacement records
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Containment-relevant because eroded social fabric degrades the wider system; rights-relevant if discrimination, exclusion, or targeted domination appears.
example: Example: A public-space renovation that increases safe cross-group interaction improves U3/D3.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether cohesion gains for some came via exclusion of others.

what_this_cell_measures: The community's shared knowledge, information access, and local expertise.
benefit_movement: Better local information access, preserved local/Indigenous knowledge, stronger civic literacy.
harm_movement: Information loss, erosion of local knowledge, misinformation spread.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: information-access measures; local-knowledge preservation records; misinformation prevalence
gate_cues: Gate classes: Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; containment-relevant where an epistemic commons is degraded. Can be rights-relevant for Indigenous knowledge.
example: Example: A program documenting local ecological knowledge with community consent improves U3/D4.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks consent and ownership of the knowledge claimed as preserved.

what_this_cell_measures: The community's collective capacity to organise, participate, and influence decisions affecting it.
benefit_movement: Stronger local voice, participation, self-organisation, and contestability.
harm_movement: Disenfranchisement, suppressed organising, exclusion from decisions.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: participation in local governance; consultation quality; association / assembly freedom
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Often rights-covered (assembly, association, participation); containment-relevant where civic capacity underpins system stability.
example: Example: A binding community-consultation requirement on local development raises U3/D5.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer tests whether participation was substantive or a procedural formality.

what_this_cell_measures: The community's shared identity, culture, dignity, and sense of collective purpose.
benefit_movement: Stronger shared identity, cultural continuity, pride, and belonging.
harm_movement: Cultural erosion, stigma, loss of identity, collective humiliation.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: cultural-participation data; heritage continuity; community-identity surveys
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; rights-relevant for cultural rights and minority protection. Soft to measure — mark uncertainty.
example: Example: Protecting a culturally significant site during redevelopment preserves U3/D6.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer separates a genuine cultural effect from a symbolic gesture.

what_this_cell_measures: The ecological condition of the community's local environment: green space, biodiversity, water, land.
benefit_movement: Restored habitat, cleaner local environment, protected green space.
harm_movement: Habitat loss, local pollution, degraded green space, contamination.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: local biodiversity / green-space data; pollution monitoring; land-use change
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Containment-relevant (local ecology supports wider systems); tail-relevant where degradation is irreversible or contamination could cascade.
example: Example: A watershed-protection rule that prevents local contamination improves U3/D7.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether 'no local effect' was measured or merely assumed.

what_this_cell_measures: An organization's operating means: finances, capital, staffing, and capacity to function and deliver.
benefit_movement: Stronger finances, capacity, staffing, and operational sustainability.
harm_movement: Insolvency risk, capacity loss, layoffs, operational decline.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: financial statements; staffing and capacity data; service-delivery metrics
gate_cues: Gate classes: Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; containment-relevant when organizational gains are extracted by externalising harm onto community, polity, or biosphere scopes.
example: Example: A funding change that stabilises a hospital's operating budget improves U4/D1.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether the organizational gain creates uncosted externalities in other cells (the classic 'operating resources up, U7 down' trap).

what_this_cell_measures: The safety of people within and affected by the organization: workers, users, and the public.
benefit_movement: Fewer injuries, safer operations, better safety culture and compliance.
harm_movement: Workplace injury, unsafe products/services, public-safety incidents.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: incident and injury rates; safety-compliance audits; near-miss reporting
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Tail Risk; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Rights-covered via labour and safety protections; tail-relevant where failure could cause catastrophic or mass-casualty events.
example: Example: A maintenance regime that cuts industrial-accident rates improves U4/D2.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether reported safety reflects outcomes or only paperwork compliance.

what_this_cell_measures: The internal relational health of the organization: trust, fairness, inclusion, and cooperation.
benefit_movement: Healthier culture, fairer treatment, reduced harassment, stronger cooperation.
harm_movement: Toxic culture, discrimination, harassment, low trust, burnout.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: staff-climate surveys; grievance and turnover data; fairness / inclusion measures
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; rights-relevant where discrimination or harassment occurs.
example: Example: An anti-harassment reform that reduces verified grievances improves U4/D3.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether culture data is independent or self-reported by leadership.

what_this_cell_measures: The organization's knowledge, data integrity, institutional memory, and learning systems.
benefit_movement: Better knowledge retention, data integrity, transparency, and learning.
harm_movement: Knowledge loss, data corruption, opacity, broken institutional memory.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: data-integrity audits; documentation completeness; knowledge-retention metrics
gate_cues: Gate classes: Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; containment-relevant where degraded knowledge systems undermine accountability or wider-system reliability.
example: Example: A records-integrity upgrade that makes decisions auditable improves U4/D4.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer tests whether claimed integrity is verifiable or asserted.

what_this_cell_measures: The meaningful autonomy, voice, and fair treatment of individuals in their organizational roles.
benefit_movement: More voice, fair process, reasonable autonomy, freedom from arbitrary treatment.
harm_movement: Arbitrary power, suppressed voice, exploitation, loss of role autonomy.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: worker-voice mechanisms; grievance outcomes; autonomy / discretion measures
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Rights-relevant via labour rights and freedom of association; otherwise ordinary.
example: Example: A grievance process with real remedy improves U4/D5.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether voice mechanisms produce outcomes or are decorative.

what_this_cell_measures: The alignment between the organization's stated purpose and its actual conduct and effects.
benefit_movement: Stronger purpose-conduct alignment, integrity, and legitimate mission delivery.
harm_movement: Mission drift, purpose-washing, hollow mandate, loss of legitimacy.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: mission-vs-outcome analysis; stakeholder-trust measures; conduct audits
gate_cues: Gate classes: Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; containment-relevant where mission decay (HOI-adjacent) hollows out the institution. Distinct from the formal HOI diagnostic.
example: Example: A governance reform that realigns conduct with mandate improves U4/D6.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether coherence is evidenced by conduct or only by restated values.

what_this_cell_measures: The environmental impact of the organization's operations: emissions, waste, resource use, land.
benefit_movement: Lower emissions/waste, reduced resource intensity, smaller harmful footprint.
harm_movement: Pollution, emissions, waste, resource depletion, ecological damage.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: emissions and waste data; resource-use intensity; environmental-compliance records
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Containment-relevant (footprint degrades wider scopes); tail-relevant where the footprint contributes to irreversible or large-scale harm. The canonical 'local win, wider loss' cell.
example: Example: A process change that cuts a plant's emissions while sustaining output improves U4/D7.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks footprint against measured externalities, not offset claims alone.

what_this_cell_measures: The polity's fiscal and material capacity: public finances, infrastructure, and provisioning.
benefit_movement: Sounder public finances, better infrastructure, sustainable provisioning.
harm_movement: Fiscal crisis, infrastructure decay, depleted public capacity.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: public-finance data; infrastructure condition indices; fiscal-sustainability metrics
gate_cues: Gate classes: Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Ordinary welfare; containment-relevant where short-term fiscal wins erode long-term public capacity.
example: Example: An infrastructure-maintenance program that prevents asset decay improves U5/D1.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether gains are sustainable or borrowed from the future.

what_this_cell_measures: The health, safety, and mortality outcomes of the whole population within a polity.
benefit_movement: Lower population mortality/morbidity, better system-wide care, stronger resilience.
harm_movement: Rising mortality, system overload, reduced care access, public-health crises.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: population mortality / morbidity; health-system capacity; health-equity gaps; outbreak surveillance
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Tail Risk; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Tail-relevant for pandemic / health-system-collapse scenarios (non-averagable); rights-relevant under right-to-health floors; otherwise ordinary welfare.
example: Example: A vaccination program that lowers population mortality improves U5/D2.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether worst-case scenarios were bounded with a tail measure, not averaged away.

what_this_cell_measures: The rule of law, due process, accountability, and perceived legitimacy of public institutions.
benefit_movement: Stronger rule of law, due process, accountability, and institutional trust.
harm_movement: Erosion of rule of law, impunity, corruption, collapse of institutional trust.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: rule-of-law indices; due-process / judicial-independence measures; corruption indicators; institutional-trust surveys
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Strongly containment-relevant: legitimacy is load-bearing for the whole system. Rights-relevant (due process); tail-relevant where collapse risks systemic instability.
example: Example: A judicial-independence safeguard that resists political capture improves U5/D3.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer tests whether legitimacy is measured independently or claimed by the institution being assessed.

what_this_cell_measures: The polity's information environment: access, transparency, free expression, and epistemic integrity.
benefit_movement: Better transparency, information access, free expression, healthier epistemic commons.
harm_movement: Censorship, opacity, disinformation, surveillance chilling, epistemic capture.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: transparency / FOI metrics; press-freedom indices; disinformation prevalence; surveillance scope
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Rights-covered (free expression, information rights); containment-relevant because a damaged epistemic commons undermines all other governance.
example: Example: An open-data and FOI reform that increases verifiable transparency improves U5/D4.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether transparency is real and usable or nominal.

what_this_cell_measures: People's ability to participate in public life, exercise rights, contest authority, and influence governance.
benefit_movement: Stronger voting access, participation, transparency, due process, and contestability.
harm_movement: Suppression, censorship, corruption, procedural exclusion, arbitrary enforcement, reduced civic voice.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: voting access and turnout; procedural-fairness measures; availability of legal remedies; consultation quality; censorship reports
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Frequently rights-covered: tied to due process, liberty, information, dignity, and civic rights — non-compensatory under NCRC. Containment-relevant for system stability.
example: Example: A reform expanding access to public hearings raises U5/D5; one that blocks lawful dissent harms it.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer tests whether civic participation is enforceable or merely nominal, and whether any group is selectively excluded.

what_this_cell_measures: Shared civic identity, dignity, social contract, and non-domination across the polity.
benefit_movement: Stronger civic dignity, inclusion, fair recognition, and a credible social contract.
harm_movement: Domination, civic humiliation, exclusionary identity, eroded social contract.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: inclusion / recognition measures; social-contract trust surveys; discrimination indicators
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Containment / Structural Viability. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Rights-relevant (dignity, non-domination, non-discrimination); containment-relevant where a fractured social contract destabilises the polity. Soft to measure.
example: Example: A reconciliation policy that credibly extends recognition to a marginalised group improves U5/D6.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer separates symbolic recognition from changes people actually experience.

what_this_cell_measures: The environmental quality and ecological sustainability managed at the polity scale.
benefit_movement: Better regional environmental quality, sustainable resource management, reduced systemic pollution.
harm_movement: Regional pollution, resource depletion, ecosystem degradation, environmental injustice.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: regional environmental monitoring; resource-stock data; pollution and emissions; environmental-justice mapping
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Tail-relevant where regional harm is irreversible or large-scale; containment-relevant; rights-relevant under environmental-justice and environmental-rights regimes.
example: Example: A regional emissions cap that prevents airshed degradation improves U5/D7.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether environmental-justice distribution was assessed, not just regional totals.

what_this_cell_measures: Humanity's shared material base: global resource stocks, critical supply chains, and common infrastructure.
benefit_movement: More sustainable global resource use, resilient supply chains, protected commons.
harm_movement: Resource depletion, supply-chain fragility, degradation of global commons.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: global resource-stock data; supply-chain resilience metrics; commons-condition indicators
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Containment-relevant and tail-relevant where depletion or fragility threatens systemic, hard-to-reverse harm at civilisational scale.
example: Example: A critical-minerals stewardship agreement that reduces depletion risk improves U6/D1.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether 'global' claims rest on global data or extrapolated local figures.

what_this_cell_measures: The safety and survival of humanity at large, including existential and catastrophic risk.
benefit_movement: Reduced catastrophic and existential risk; stronger global safety and resilience.
harm_movement: Increased existential, pandemic, conflict, or technological catastrophic risk.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: catastrophic-risk assessments; biosecurity / nuclear-risk indicators; conflict-escalation data
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Tail Risk; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Primarily tail-relevant: catastrophic and existential risk is non-averagable and bounded under TRC, never traded against ordinary welfare. Rights-relevant at the right-to-life floor.
example: Example: A biosecurity protocol that lowers engineered-pandemic risk improves U6/D2.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks that tail risk was bounded with a worst-case measure and not diluted by expected-value framing.

what_this_cell_measures: The capacity of humanity to coordinate, cooperate, and maintain peaceful, stable relations at scale.
benefit_movement: Stronger global cooperation, conflict reduction, durable coordination institutions.
harm_movement: Breakdown of cooperation, arms races, institutional collapse, escalating conflict.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: international-cooperation indices; conflict / treaty-compliance data; coordination-institution health
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Containment-relevant (cooperation underpins global stability); tail-relevant where breakdown risks large-scale conflict.
example: Example: A verification regime that sustains an arms-control treaty improves U6/D3.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether cooperation is durable or a fragile short-term arrangement.

what_this_cell_measures: Humanity's accumulated knowledge, science, and the integrity and safety of its knowledge systems.
benefit_movement: Knowledge preservation, scientific progress, epistemic integrity, responsible knowledge stewardship.
harm_movement: Knowledge loss, scientific capture, epistemic collapse, or proliferation of dangerous knowledge.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: scientific-integrity measures; knowledge-preservation status; research-governance indicators
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Containment-relevant; tail-relevant in two directions — catastrophic loss of knowledge, and dangerous diffusion of harmful capability.
example: Example: An open-but-governed research framework that preserves integrity while limiting dangerous diffusion improves U6/D4.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether knowledge benefits were weighed against misuse and proliferation pathways.

what_this_cell_measures: Humanity's capacity for self-determination and legitimate collective decision-making at the species scale.
benefit_movement: Stronger legitimate global agency, fair representation, and self-determination.
harm_movement: Concentration of unaccountable power, disenfranchisement of peoples, loss of collective self-determination.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: representation / participation in global governance; power-concentration indicators; self-determination measures
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Containment / Structural Viability. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Rights-relevant (self-determination); containment-relevant where illegitimate concentration destabilises the system. Measurement is contested — mark uncertainty.
example: Example: A governance reform giving affected populations real voice in a global regime improves U6/D5.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer tests whether 'collective' agency includes the marginalised or only powerful actors.

what_this_cell_measures: Humanity's shared sense of meaning, moral direction, and long-term orientation toward flourishing.
benefit_movement: Stronger shared purpose, long-term orientation, intergenerational responsibility.
harm_movement: Nihilism, short-termism, loss of shared direction, intergenerational betrayal.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: long-term-orientation indicators; intergenerational-equity measures; qualitative analysis
gate_cues: Gate classes: Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Mostly ordinary/aspirational; containment-relevant where short-termism erodes long-term stability. Inherently soft — mark uncertainty and avoid overclaiming.
example: Example: A long-horizon institution (e.g. a future-generations commissioner) can support U6/D6.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer flags this cell as especially prone to rhetoric and demands concrete mechanisms.

what_this_cell_measures: The condition of planetary systems that support human civilisation and coordinated managing intelligence.
benefit_movement: Reduced emissions, improved climate stability, lower systemic ecological risk, stronger global resilience.
harm_movement: Increased climate risk, global pollution, destabilised food/water systems, irreversible planetary degradation.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: emissions data; climate models; planetary-boundary metrics; global food/water-security projections
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Often catastrophe-relevant: may trigger TRC where irreversible or large-scale harm is plausible. Containment-relevant as a system-stability check.
example: Example: A high-emissions infrastructure choice may harm U6/D7 even when it benefits a local economy (U3/D1 or U4/D1).
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether irreversibility and worst-case bounds were modelled, not just expected outcomes.

what_this_cell_measures: The biosphere's foundational resources that sustain life: soil, fresh water, clean air, fertility.
benefit_movement: Protected or restored soil, water, and air; sustained natural-resource base.
harm_movement: Soil loss, water depletion, air degradation, exhaustion of life-support systems.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: soil-health data; freshwater-stock and quality; air-quality baselines; resource-renewal rates
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Tail-relevant where depletion is irreversible or threatens collapse of life-support systems; containment-relevant. Distinct from U4/D1 'operating resources'.
example: Example: An aquifer-protection rule that prevents irreversible groundwater loss improves U7/D1.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether renewal rates, not just current stocks, were assessed.

what_this_cell_measures: The health, function, and viability of ecosystems and the species within them.
benefit_movement: Healthier, functioning ecosystems; recovering species and habitats.
harm_movement: Ecosystem dysfunction, species decline, habitat collapse, trophic breakdown.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: ecosystem-function indicators; species-population trends; habitat-condition assessments
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Tail-relevant where collapse or extinction is plausible and irreversible; containment-relevant as ecosystems underpin wider scopes.
example: Example: A fisheries policy that lets a collapsing stock recover improves U7/D2.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether ecosystem-function evidence exists or only a single charismatic indicator.

what_this_cell_measures: The integrity of relationships and interdependencies among living systems and between humans and nature.
benefit_movement: Restored ecological relationships, sustainable human-nature interactions, protected interdependencies.
harm_movement: Disrupted food webs, broken ecological relationships, harmful human-nature dynamics.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: trophic / food-web indicators; interaction-network data; human-impact assessments
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Containment-relevant: a local win that severs ecological relationships can fail containment even with strong U4/D1 gains; tail-relevant where cascades are plausible.
example: Example: A factory expansion that damages a watershed may fail containment via U7/D3 even while improving U4/D1.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether relational/cascade effects were modelled or ignored as 'no direct effect'.

what_this_cell_measures: Humanity's understanding and monitoring of ecological systems, including baseline and early-warning data.
benefit_movement: Better ecological monitoring, baselines, early-warning capacity, and stewardship knowledge.
harm_movement: Monitoring gaps, lost baselines, ecological ignorance, blind spots before thresholds.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: monitoring-coverage data; baseline-completeness; early-warning-system status
gate_cues: Gate classes: Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Explicitly elevated. Interpretation: Containment-relevant: poor ecological knowledge undermines the ability to detect tipping points. Often the cell most affected by the 0-vs-unknown distinction.
example: Example: An expanded biodiversity-monitoring network that fills baseline gaps improves U7/D4.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks that absent ecological data is marked unknown, not scored as 0 ('no effect').

what_this_cell_measures: The biosphere's capacity to absorb shocks, adapt, and recover from disturbance.
benefit_movement: Greater ecological resilience, redundancy, and recovery capacity.
harm_movement: Loss of resilience, reduced redundancy, approach to tipping points and regime shifts.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: resilience / redundancy indicators; recovery-rate data; threshold-proximity assessments
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Tail-relevant where loss of resilience brings irreversible regime shifts; containment-relevant as resilience buffers all scopes.
example: Example: Restoring wetland buffers that absorb flood shocks improves U7/D5.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer asks whether proximity to thresholds was assessed, not just current condition.

what_this_cell_measures: The continuity and persistence of life and biodiversity over time, including irreversibility of loss.
benefit_movement: Protected biodiversity, prevented extinctions, sustained continuity of life.
harm_movement: Species extinction, irreversible biodiversity loss, broken continuity of lineages.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: extinction-risk (e.g. red-list) data; biodiversity-trend indices; irreversibility assessments
gate_cues: Gate classes: Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Strongly tail-relevant: extinction is the paradigm of irreversible, non-averagable harm under TRC; containment-relevant.
example: Example: A habitat-corridor program that prevents a species' extinction improves U7/D6.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether irreversibility was treated as a tail constraint, not a discountable cost.

what_this_cell_measures: The overall health, resilience, diversity, and continuity of ecosystems as living support systems.
benefit_movement: Habitat restoration, biodiversity protection, improved ecological resilience, reduced pollution.
harm_movement: Habitat destruction, species loss, ecosystem collapse, pollution, soil/water degradation.
indicators_evidence: Evidence: biodiversity indices; habitat-area data; water/soil quality; ecosystem-resilience measures; ecological monitoring
gate_cues: Gate classes: Rights Floor; Tail Risk; Containment / Structural Viability; Ordinary welfare. Uncertainty: Standard assessment. Interpretation: Often containment-relevant and sometimes catastrophe-relevant; may relate to ecological-integrity rights where recognised (e.g. rights of nature).
example: Example: A factory expansion that damages a watershed may fail containment even when it improves U4/D1.
reviewer_check: Reviewer check: A reviewer checks whether integrity is evidenced by ecosystem-level data or inferred from a single metric.
